subject: ArborEdge renewal — capacity amendment & sizing recommendation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@arboredge.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-15T14:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal planning — quick check on Q3 utilization and bump options

Hi Elena,

Hope you’re doing well. As we approach ArborEdge’s 12/01 renewal, I pulled a short utilization summary for your Dedicated cluster and wanted to share a couple of low-friction options to avoid any mid-quarter throttles. Short summary attached (ARB-Q3-utilization-summary.csv).

What I’m seeing: a sustained 68% slot-level utilization across peak hours with four discrete daily spikes that push queue latency above our 95th pct SLO. Those spikes correlate to your nightly ensemble runs and an occasional inference campaign. Based on that, there are two sensible paths:

1) Soft top-up: add a 32-GPU burst tranche (30-day auto-bill) and keep current commit — fastest to implement, good for seasonal bursts.
2) Capacity amendment: increase dedicated commit from 64 -> 96 GPUs with a graduated billing schedule and a 10% unit discount — best for predictable latency and lowering per-token unit cost.

I can put together a redline amendment (option 2) and a short-term burst activation quote (option 1). Which would you prefer to evaluate first? If useful, I can also propose an autoscale safety floor that prevents the nightly spikes from impacting tail latency.

Thanks,
Hannah

--

Hannah, thank you for the fast analysis and the CSV — that was helpful. A couple quick questions before we escalate to procurement:

- Can you provide an expected monthly spend delta for both options (soft top-up vs commit increase)? We need a ballpark before the budget review.
- What impact should we expect on 95th/99th pct latency if we go to 96 GPUs? Our application is sensitive to tail latency.
- Is there a minimum commitment period if we do the 96-GPU amendment? Our procurement prefers 6/12 month terms.

I’m looping in procurement for evaluation. We have a renewal call next Thursday 10/22 — would love to have a simple recommendation and a PDF amendment to review.

- a short operational play: autoscale floor + 32-GPU burst buffer for peak nights during the first 30 days of migration.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: ArborEdge renewal — capacity questions from Elena (ARB-7892)

Quick analysis below (high level). Karthik — feel free to correct the kernel-level assumptions.

Baseline: 64 dedicated GPUs, sustained slot utilization ~68% in peak window, tail pressure from four nightly campaigns (spikes ~3x baseline).

Option A — Soft top-up (32-GPU burst tranche):
- Time to implement: 24h (enable burst tranche + billing)
- Expected tail impact: reduce 95th pct latency by ~20-30% during spike windows, little change to 99th pct because bursts can saturate if multiple campaigns overlap.
- Estimated monthly cost delta (ballpark): +$28k/month (on-demand-style tranche)

Option B — Commit increase 64 -> 96 GPUs (preferred):
- Time to implement: 7–10 days (amendment + provisioning + canary traffic shift)
- Expected tail impact: reduce 95th pct latency by ~45-55% and 99th pct by ~25-35% based on current KV cache hit rates and request-size distribution.
- Pricing: propose a graduated 12-month schedule or a 6-month trial price with a higher per-unit rate. Ballpark delta: +$62k/month at current list, with proposed 10% unit discount for annual commit.
- Operational recommendation: enable a persistent autoscale floor (reserve ~8% of cluster capacity) + 32-GPU burst buffer for the first 30 days to smooth transition.

Attachment: redwood-sizing-options.xlsx (contains model assumptions and Monte Carlo sims).

TL;DR: Recommend Option B with a 6-month pilot amendment (reduces churn risk) and the 30-day burst buffer enabled during rollout.

Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-20T09:30:00Z
Subject: ARB-7892 — proposed amendment (6-mo pilot) and implementation plan

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is the proposed amendment (ARB-7892-dedicated-amendment-v2.pdf) and the sizing workbook. Summary below:

What we propose (6-month pilot):
- Commit: increase Dedicated commit from 64 -> 96 GPUs (effective on sign).
- Pricing: pilot rate = current list * (96/64) with no annual discount for pilot; follow-on option for 12-month commit with 10% unit discount.
- Safety measures: persistent autoscale floor (~8% of cluster), immediate 32-GPU burst buffer for the first 30 days, monitoring dashboard with token-level latency alerts and rollback policy.
- Expected impact: 45-55% improvement on 95th pct latency and 25-35% on 99th pct during peak windows (per Ben’s analysis).

Next steps:
1) Procurement review (cc’d) — confirm term preference (6 vs 12 months) and billing contact.
2) If 6-month pilot accepted, sign the attached amendment and we’ll provision within 7–10 days and enable the burst buffer concurrently.
3) We’ll schedule a technical cutover runbook review with Karthik and Ben.
